CNA text: missing input validation in MP_REACH_NLRI on FRRouting stable/10.0 to stable/10.6 lets an authenticated peer cause DoS with a crafted UPDATE. GHSA-m357-6hwr-7w53 has withdrawn_at null; GitHub withdrawn_at is not used as authority.

Source: authenticated BGP UPDATE with MP_REACH_NLRI carrying an IPv4/VPNv4 next-hop. At fix parent 5c4ca8895b3a7ce7e9f5f58548c33db3950fd170, bgpd/bgp_attr.c bgp_mp_reach_parse case BGP_ATTR_NHLEN_VPNV4 falls through into BGP_ATTR_NHLEN_IPV4 and stream_get copies four bytes into attr->mp_nexthop_global_in with no ipv4_martian check. The ordinary NEXT_HOP path in the same file (bgp_attr_nexthop_valid) already rejects ipv4_martian(&attr->nexthop) unless allow_martian.

Sink: bgpd/bgp_route.c bgp_update_martian_nexthop at 5c4ca8895b3a7ce7e9f5f58548c33db3950fd170 returns false (treat as valid) when safi is not SAFI_UNICAST/SAFI_MULTICAST/SAFI_EVPN, so SAFI_MPLS_VPN/VPNv4 never hits the later ipv4_unicast_valid check on mp_nexthop_global_in. bgp_update() then continues past the 'next hop check' call at that function, installing an unusable martian next-hop. Direct fix 8102a8aeceb9f86fdfe1f80cd77080522bab69c8 adds parser-level ipv4_martian(&attr->mp_nexthop_global_in) and returns BGP_ATTR_PARSE_WITHDRAW.

findings: CVE-2026-37458 is a real published vulnerability: MP_REACH_NLRI IPv4/VPNv4 next-hop is copied without martian validation, and later bgp_update_martian_nexthop skips non-unicast/multicast/EVPN SAFIs, so a crafted authenticated UPDATE can accept an unusable next-hop (DoS).

Smallest surviving public BIC is parentless initial revision 718e3744195351130f4ce7dbe0613f4b3e23df93, which already first-writes both the IPv4 (len 4) and VPNv4 (len 12) stream_get paths into mp_nexthop_global_in with no martian check.

Direct fix is 8102a8aeceb9f86fdfe1f80cd77080522bab69c8 (PR 21075), with equivalent backports 031bdbf5b6832c31048111b56807769236ac85e2 (frr-10.5.4+), 638ee72802b159056234400037421cc5749185be (frr-10.6.0+), and fed7d6dde1f15ed5dc2c7caedcfcb51112f93a39 (frr-10.4.4+).
